clue.text: Hear blade I had is dirty

indicators.note: hear asks the solver to say the word for blade out loud and keep only its sound

parts.note: a blade, as a weapon, is a sword
I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: Someone listening to a knife-wielder's confession: the weapon they had is filthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' says SWORD is wanted only as it sounds, spelt SORD; the definition 'is dirty' works as an adjective phrase with the link to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sordid describes something squalid and grubby, literally or morally.

clue.text: Unconcealed rage may exhaust

parts.note: overt means open and not hidden
ire is anger or rage

explanation.surface: Open fury can wear a person out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may' is a link between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtire someone is to tire them beyond endurance, wearing them out.

clue.text: No progress possible here in home security feature

explanation.surface: Stalemate over a burglar-proof fitting at home.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is an impasse in negotiations; the other is a lock on a front door; 'in' links them.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalemate where neither side can advance is a deadlock; and a deadbolt lock fitted to a door is also called that.

clue.text: Log being at sea

parts.note: reads like a ship's record kept on a voyage, but describes a piece of timber floating adrift on the waves

explanation.surface: A ship's journal written during a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Log' suggests a captain's record; it is a piece of wood, and 'at sea' hints at adrift.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber washed ashore or floating in the ocean is called this.

clue.text: Painter calling for his dog?

explanation.surface: An artist summoning his pet by blowing a shrill note.
explanation.walkthrough: James McNeill Whistler was the American painter of 'Whistler's Mother'; the second reading is anyone who whistles to call a dog, signalled by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The American-born artist Whistler is the painter; and someone blowing a summons to a hound is literally one who whistles.

clue.text: Appealing, get defeated occasionally — that's the way it goes

parts.note: winsome means charming or appealing
to be beaten sometimes is to lose some

explanation.surface: A charming loser shrugs off the odd setback philosophically.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word is an adjective giving the first piece, though it reads as part of the shrug.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses resignation: success and failure both come along in life.

clue.text: Seafood gives a sort of edge

explanation.surface: A dish of shellfish served with a decorative rim.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the shellfish; the other is a wavy ornamental border; 'gives' links them.
explanation.definitionFit: A bivalve mollusc eaten as seafood; also a curved decorative edging copied from its shell.

clue.text: Where washing hangs, including miss halliwell's smalls

indicators.note: including means the clothes line holds the singer's name within it

parts.note: laundry is hung out on a line to dry
Geri Halliwell was Ginger Spice in the Spice Girls

explanation.surface: A pop star's underwear pegged out on the washing line.
explanation.walkthrough: SMALLS is British slang for underwear; Geri Halliwell is a former Spice Girls singer. The surface hides 'including' as the container signal inside a laundry scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Women's underwear is lingerie, the same items as smalls.

clue.text: Relaxed, being sent money

explanation.surface: A person calm after getting paid.
explanation.walkthrough: To remit a penalty is to relax or cancel it; to remit money is to send it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule remitted is eased or lessened; funds remitted have been transferred by post or bank.

clue.text: Funny oriental cousin?

indicators.note: funny suggests something odd or peculiar, so the letters of the next word are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: Asking whether an amusing Eastern person is a member of the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' rearranges ORIENTAL; the question mark admits that a cousin is only one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is one example of a family member, a kinsman.

clue.text: Bottle and something to read taken by miners

parts.note: a magazine, shortened to mag, is something to read
the NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers

explanation.surface: Colliery workers picking up a bottle and some reading matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUM is Britain's National Union of Mineworkers, the miners' trade union; 'taken by' just sets the second piece after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum is a large wine bottle holding twice the standard measure.

clue.text: Dagger fired back in fight

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the word for a fight

parts.note: a set-to is a brief fight or scrap

indicators.note: back says the word meaning fired is read from right to left

parts.note: a fire that has been fired is lit

explanation.surface: A blade is shot back during a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' signals a reversal of the word for fired, and 'in' signals the container; 'fired' looks like a gunshot but is the past tense of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short thin-bladed knife, a type of slim stabbing weapon.

clue.text: Able to speak well of hospital department after illness

indicators.note: after places the hospital department behind the illness in the answer

parts.note: influenza, flu for short, is an illness
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A patient recovering from sickness speaks highly of the hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'speak well of' as praise; the definition stops at 'well', 'of' is a link, and 'after' orders the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A fluent speaker talks smoothly and articulately, without hesitation.

clue.text: Concocted what might get swallowed?

explanation.surface: A made-up story that someone might fall for.
explanation.walkthrough: Concocted is invented, as a tale; food that has been prepared over heat is what gets eaten, and 'swallowed' also hints at being believed.
explanation.definitionFit: To invent an excuse is to cook it up; prepared hot food is cooked and then eaten.

clue.text: What we've all agreed to be

definitions.text: What we've all agreed to be

parts.words: What we've all agreed to be
parts.note: reads like a group deciding a plan, but describes the state of being in complete agreement with no dissent

explanation.surface: A group settling on a plan together.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue simply describes total consensus.
explanation.definitionFit: Unanimous means in full agreement, with every member voting the same way.

clue.text: Kiss Gregory?

explanation.surface: Asking an actor named Gregory for a smooch.
explanation.walkthrough: Gregory Peck was the Hollywood star of 'To Kill a Mockingbird'; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick light kiss is a peck; and the actor Gregory had that surname.

clue.text: Get tot down

parts.note: sounds like writing a small sum or a drink down, but means settling a small child for the night in its cot

explanation.surface: An instruction to note a small figure or swallow a dram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' could be a sum or a dram of spirits; here it is a toddler, and 'down' means to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Parents settle a young child for sleep by tucking it in at bedtime.

clue.text: About to go into plans for cathedral

indicators.note: to go into means the word for about is placed inside the word for plans

parts.note: charts are maps or plans
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Approaching a project to design a great church.
explanation.walkthrough: Chartres is a French city famed for its Gothic cathedral; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The great Gothic cathedral of Chartres, south-west of Paris, is known by its town's name.

clue.text: Being induced to embrace women's indecent

indicators.note: to embrace means one word holds the abbreviation for women within it

parts.note: induced or persuaded, as someone led into something
W is the standard abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Being lured into an improper embrace with women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to embrace' puts W inside LED; 'Being' just joins the pieces to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lewd is crude and obscene, offending sexual propriety.

clue.text: But it's not the only twelvemonth containing spring

definitions.text: But it's not the only twelvemonth containing spring

parts.words: But it's not the only twelvemonth containing spring
parts.note: seems to say every year has a springtime, but spring means a jump, and the twelvemonth with an extra day is the one that contains it

explanation.surface: A remark that every year has a season of new growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' suggests the season; it is a jump, and every year has a spring season, which is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A year with 29 February, occurring every fourth year, is named for jumping a day.

clue.text: Liking many novel experiences, we will dare to be different

parts.note: we will contracts to we'll, spelt without the apostrophe

indicators.note: to be different asks for the letters of dare to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Adventurous types resolve to break from the norm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel experiences' sounds like adventures; it means books. 'to be different' rearranges DARE into READ.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookish person who has gone through many books is learned through literature.

clue.text: Recommend lawyer

explanation.surface: A barrister being endorsed.
explanation.walkthrough: As a verb the word means to urge or support; as a noun it is a legal professional, especially in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate a plan is to back it publicly; an advocate is a counsel who pleads cases in court.

clue.text: Real's an exceptional football team

indicators.note: exceptional suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: Praise for the Spanish club Real Madrid as outstanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Real' looks like the Spanish club Real Madrid; 'exceptional' rearranges REALS AN. Arsenal is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a north London Premier League club.

clue.text: Bird takes most of the water-plant

indicators.note: most of means the short word loses its final letter

parts.note: a rush is a grass-like plant growing in wet ground

explanation.surface: A bird grabs nearly all the reeds by the pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the final E of 'the' to leave TH.
explanation.definitionFit: The song thrush and mistle thrush are common songbirds.

clue.text: Sample of views of those leaving the station

definitions.text: Sample of views of those leaving the station

parts.words: Sample of views of those leaving the station
parts.note: sounds like questioning passengers at a railway stop, but the station is a polling station, and the survey is of voters as they depart

explanation.surface: Surveying the opinions of commuters coming off a train platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'station' suggests trains; the station meant is a polling station on election day.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollsters question voters as they come out of polling booths to predict the result.

clue.text: Making holes is tedious

explanation.surface: Drilling holes is dull work.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is drilling; the other is dull and uninteresting.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill bores holes, so the act is boring; dull talk is also boring.

clue.text: Attached to the car that clocks up the miles!

definitions.text: Attached to the car that clocks up the miles!

parts.words: Attached to the car that clocks up the miles!
parts.note: reads like someone devoted to a high-mileage vehicle, but describes the dashboard instrument fitted to a car that records distance travelled

explanation.surface: Fond of a well-used car with plenty of miles on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attached to' looks like affection for an old banger; it means fixed to the vehicle, and 'clocks up' describes the instrument itself.
explanation.definitionFit: This dashboard instrument records total distance travelled by a vehicle.

clue.text: Lose out in engagement, becoming lonely

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the word for an engagement

parts.note: a date is an engagement or appointment

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of lose are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: Losing at a romantic meeting leaves someone feeling forlorn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the first word into ESOL, and 'in' signals the container, split after the first letter; 'becoming' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolate means bleak and forlorn, abandoned and alone.

clue.text: A fast walk — that's the way to travel

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to ride is to travel on a horse or vehicle

explanation.surface: Walking briskly is recommended as the best way of getting about.
explanation.walkthrough: ST stands for street, a common crossword way.
explanation.definitionFit: A stride is a long brisk step, a purposeful gait.
